course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Decimals, Percentages and Rounding
unit.blurb: Multiplying and dividing by powers of 10, calculating with decimals, compound percentages, and upper and lower bounds.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Multiply and divide numbers by 10 to any positive or negative power, e.g. 10³, 10⁻², and by 0.1 and 0.01.

O2.t: Multiply and divide by decimals, using estimation to check answers.

O3.t: Understand compound percentages, e.g. a 10% increase followed by a 10% decrease, and calculate repeated percentage change.

O4.t: Find the upper and lower bounds of a number rounded to a given degree of accuracy.

sections.title: Multiplying and dividing by powers of 10

p: Multiplying by 10ⁿ moves the digits **n places to the left** (the number gets bigger); dividing by 10ⁿ moves them n places to the **right**.
10⁻¹ = 0.1 and 10⁻² = 0.01. So **multiplying by 0.1 is the same as dividing by 10**, and dividing by 0.01 is the same as multiplying by 100.

p: An increase of r% means multiplying by **1 + r/100**. A decrease of r% means multiplying by **1 − r/100**. So +15% is × 1.15 and −8% is × 0.92.
For changes one after another, **multiply the multipliers**. A 10% increase then a 10% decrease is × 1.1 × 0.9 = × 0.99 – a 1% decrease overall, NOT 'no change'.

p: A rounded number could have been any value in a range. If a length is 8 cm **to the nearest cm**, the real length is at least 7.5 cm (the **lower bound**) and less than 8.5 cm (the **upper bound**).
The bounds are **half a unit** below and above. We write 7.5 ≤ l < 8.5.

p: For 8 cm to the nearest cm the upper bound is 8.5 cm, not 8.4 cm or 8.49 cm – values up to (but not including) 8.5 round to 8.
